name: acme/servicedesk-mcp-pack
description: Example MCP tool pack for iTop, built on altioo-mcp.
_comment_mcp_sdk: mcp/sdk is a REAL RUNTIME dependency of this pack: the tools below type-hint
ToolAnnotations and throw ToolCallException, and both have to resolve when a
client calls them. It is nevertheless in require-dev, and that is not a
mislabelling - it is where the dependency is satisfied from. altioo-mcp
vendors the SDK and loads it from its own datamodel array, and iTop includes
a module's datamodel files after those of the modules it depends on, so
Mcp\* is already registered by the time anything here is autoloaded.
Shipping a second copy is what has to be avoided, and 'install it then delete
vendor/mcp before packaging' does not do it: classmap-authoritative dumps
every class it found into autoload_classmap.php, so the entries survive the
deletion, point at files that are gone, and the first call fatals on a
missing include. require-dev keeps the SDK out of the production dump
entirely, which is the only version of this that is safe.
Pin the same constraint the base vendors - MCPHelper::SDK_CONSTRAINT - so
that what you compile against is what will be loaded.
_comment_autoload_dev: ContractTest declares this namespace, and without it here `composer test`
finds the file and cannot autoload the class. autoload-dev never reaches
the production dump, so it costs an installed instance nothing.
The base extension is deliberately NOT a dependency. Its ElementContract
is what the suite imports, and it is resolved the way everything else
from the base is resolved at runtime - through the autoloader that is
already registered. tests/php-unit-tests/bootstrap.php requires it from
beside this module under extensions/. Requiring the base here instead
would vendor a second copy of it, and of mcp/sdk with it, which is the
one thing the comment above is about.
_comment_autoload: Both settings are load-bearing, and neither is the composer default.
iTop's InterfaceDiscovery enumerates candidate classes by reading
leaves that file essentially empty, so a provider in src/ is never
discovered - it registers only if register.php names it explicitly, and any
class the pack fails to autoload fails silently as 'not found'.
